rows.title: New CT budget leaves huge gap one year down the road
rows.standfirst: Nearly $700M in temporary money, most of which goes to ongoing costs, will prop up CT’s budget in the next fiscal year — and then go away.

rows.title: Unions blast Lamont, consultants over UConn hospital privatization
rows.standfirst: Union officials say a consultant’s report understated John Dempsey Hospital’s role in the community and unfairly compared it to big networks.

rows.title: $74M bond for Community Investment Fund gets Lamont’s OK
rows.standfirst: The bond will fund projects including a $250,000 recreation master plan in Plainfield and $8.7 million for affordable housing in Hamden.

rows.title: Lamont administration could cut town aid but expects it won’t
rows.standfirst: Republicans questioned whether Democrats were putting local aid at risk through a hastily crafted provision to appease the administration.

rows.title: CT diesel tax to jump 3 cents after yearlong freeze
rows.standfirst: CT’s trucking industry will face a small tax hike next month when the state tax on diesel fuel goes up slightly more than 3 cents per gallon.

rows.title: CT savings program drives another $1 billion-plus surplus
rows.standfirst: Some CT lawmakers say the ‘volatile’ revenue that the fiscal guardrails collect — and that lawmakers can’t spend — is actually very stable.

rows.title: CT Treasurer Russell talks divestment, finances at ‘In the Room’
rows.standfirst: For CT Mirror’s ‘In the Room’ series, Russell touched on CT’s investments in Israel, its history of divestment, and its ‘baby bonds’ program.
